+---
+title: Pi Agent Integration Guide
+author: chaojixinren
+date: 2026-07-01
+tags:
+  - integration
+  - pi-agent
+  - coding-agent
+  - agent
+lang: en-US
+---
+
+# Pi Agent Integration Guide
+
+[中文文档](../../zh/guide/integrations/pi-agent.md)
+
+Run the [Pi coding agent](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent)
+— a terminal-native AI coding agent — inside CubeSandbox MicroVMs. This guide
+covers image build, key injection, egress control, and snapshot-based session
+persistence, and pairs with the runnable
+[`examples/pi-agent-integration`](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/tree/master/examples/pi-agent-integration)
+project.
+
+## Integration Target and Version
+
+| Component | Version |
+|---|---|
+| Pi coding agent | `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` (pinned via `--build-arg PI_VERSION=x.y.z`) |
+| Node.js | 24 (installed via NodeSource) |
+| CubeSandbox base image | `ghcr.io/tencentcloud/cubesandbox-base:2026.16` |
+| E2B SDK (host driver) | `e2b` (latest) |
+| CubeSandbox platform | `>= 0.3.0` (pause/resume) / `>= 0.4.0` (CubeEgress credential vault) |
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- A running CubeSandbox deployment; CubeAPI reachable at `http://<node>:3000`.
+- `cubemastercli` on `$PATH`, connected to the cluster.
+- Docker on the build workstation, plus a registry the Cube nodes can pull from.
+- An LLM provider API key. Anthropic is the default; any Anthropic-compatible or
+  OpenAI-compatible endpoint works via `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` / provider env.
+- Python 3.10+ for the host driver scripts.
+
+## Why Run Pi Inside a Sandbox
+
+Pi is a terminal agent that edits files, runs commands, and installs packages.
+Running it directly on a workstation blends the agent's blast radius with your
+dev environment. Running it inside CubeSandbox gives you:
+
+| Concern | CubeSandbox provides |
+|---|---|
+| **Isolation** | KVM MicroVM per session, dedicated guest kernel |
+| **Reproducibility** | Every session boots from the same template snapshot |
+| **Fast spin-up** | Sub-60 ms cold start, so N-parallel agents are cheap |
+| **Long tasks** | `sandbox.pause()` snapshots VM + rootfs; resume later |
+| **Key hygiene** | CubeEgress injects the auth header on the wire — the VM never sees the real key |
+| **Egress audit** | Every request to the LLM API is recorded in the egress audit log |
+
+## Integration Steps
+
+### 1. Build the template image
+
+The image stacks Node.js 24 and the Pi CLI on top of `cubesandbox-base`, so
+envd is already listening on `:49983`.
+
+```dockerfile
+# examples/pi-agent-integration/Dockerfile (excerpt)
+ARG CUBE_BASE_IMAGE=ghcr.io/tencentcloud/cubesandbox-base:2026.16
+FROM ${CUBE_BASE_IMAGE}
+
+ARG NODE_MAJOR=24
+ARG PI_VERSION=0.80.3
+
+RUN apt-get update \
+    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
+        ca-certificates curl git gnupg jq less procps python3 python3-pip ripgrep \
+    && curl -fsSL "https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_${NODE_MAJOR}.x" | bash - \
+    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends nodejs \
+    && npm install -g --ignore-scripts "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@${PI_VERSION}" \
+    && pi --version \
+    && npm cache clean --force \
+    && rm -rf /root/.npm /var/lib/apt/lists/*
+
+WORKDIR /workspace
+EXPOSE 49983
+```
+
+Build and push:
+
+```bash
+docker build --platform linux/amd64 \
+  -t <your-registry>/pi-agent-cube:latest \
+  examples/pi-agent-integration
+docker push <your-registry>/pi-agent-cube:latest
+```
+
+### 2. Register as a Cube template
+
+```bash
+cubemastercli tpl create-from-image \
+  --image <your-registry>/pi-agent-cube:latest \
+  --writable-layer-size 4G \
+  --expose-port 49983 \
+  --probe       49983 \
+  --probe-path  /health
+
+cubemastercli tpl watch --job-id <job_id>
+```
+
+Once the job reaches `READY`, note the `template_id` — you pass it to every
+`Sandbox.create()` call. `4G` writable layer suits medium tasks; bump to `8G+`
+if the agent installs large toolchains.
+
+### 3. Wire up the host driver
+
+```bash
+cd examples/pi-agent-integration
+cp .env.example .env
+# fill in E2B_API_URL, CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID, and your provider key
+pip install -r requirements.txt
+```
+
+| Variable | Where it flows | Notes |
+|---|---|---|
+| `E2B_API_URL` | Local process | CubeAPI address (`http://<node>:3000`) |
+| `E2B_API_KEY` | Local process | Any non-empty string in local dev |
+| `CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID` | `Sandbox.create(template=...)` | From step 2 |
+| `PI_PROVIDER` / `PI_MODEL` | Pi CLI flags | Provider and model selection |
+| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | `envs=...` (direct) or CubeEgress inject (vault) | Provider key |
+| `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` | Passed into the exec env | Anthropic-compatible gateways (e.g. DeepSeek) |
+| `PI_LLM_HOST` | `network_policy.py` | LLM host allowed under default-deny egress |
+
+### 4. Runtime Configuration and API Key Injection
+
+The Pi command is built headlessly with `--print` (process the prompt and exit,
+no TUI), an explicit provider/model, and `--mode json` so the host can capture a
+machine-readable JSONL event stream. `--approve` trusts the project-local files
+in the sandbox for this run, and the prompt is the trailing positional argument.
+Two key-flow flavors share the same template:
+
+**Direct flavor** — forward the key per command. `e2b`'s `commands.run(envs=...)`
+puts the environment into the exec envelope, not into a persistent file inside
+the VM, so the key lives only for the lifetime of that command:
+
+```python
+result = sandbox.commands.run(
+    "cd /workspace && pi --print --mode json --provider anthropic "
+    "--model claude-sonnet-4-6 --approve 'do something'",
+    envs={"ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": key},
+    user="root",
+    timeout=900,
+)
+```
+
+**Vault flavor** — keep the key out of the VM entirely (see step 6).
+
+### 5. Session Persistence (pause / resume)
+
+```bash
+python resume_pi_agent.py
+```
+
+This mirrors the [snapshot / clone / rollback](../snapshot-rollback-clone.md)
+engine at the SDK layer:
+
+- `sandbox.pause()` snapshots the running VM (memory + rootfs) and frees compute.
+- `Sandbox.connect(sandbox_id)` resumes with `/workspace`, Pi's state directory
+  (`/root/.pi/agent`), and every other file intact.
+
+> **Lifecycle caveat:** manage the sandbox lifecycle with `try/finally`, not a
+> `with Sandbox.create(...)` context manager. On `__exit__` the context manager
+> kills the sandbox, which would undo the pause. The example creates the sandbox
+> explicitly and only calls `sandbox.kill()` in `finally`.
+
+```python
+sandbox = Sandbox.create(template=template_id, timeout=1800)
+try:
+    run_turn(sandbox, prompt_1)          # writes /workspace/plan.md
+    sandbox_id = sandbox.pause() or sandbox.sandbox_id
+    sandbox = Sandbox.connect(sandbox_id)
+    assert_state_survived(sandbox)       # /workspace + /root/.pi/agent intact
+    run_turn(sandbox, prompt_2)          # continues the work
+finally:
+    sandbox.kill()
+```
+
+### 6. Network and Egress Policy (credential vault)
+
+`network_policy.py` demonstrates the recommended pattern for shared clusters:
+default-deny egress plus on-the-wire key injection.
+
+```python
+rules = [
+    {
+        "name": "allow_anthropic_llm",
+        "match": {"scheme": "https", "sni": "api.anthropic.com", "host": "api.anthropic.com"},
+        "action": {
+            "allow": True,
+            "audit": "metadata",
+            "inject": [
+                {"header": "x-api-key", "secret": ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, "format": "${SECRET}"},
+                {"header": "anthropic-version", "secret": "2023-06-01"},
+            ],
+        },
+    },
+]
+
+sandbox = Sandbox.create(
+    template=CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID,
+    allow_internet_access=True,
+    network={"rules": rules},
+)

review_comments.body:
**Critical: `allow_internet_access=True` defeats the intended default-deny egress.**

From the [network policy docs](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/blob/master/docs/guide/network-policy.md):

> `allow_internet_access` — When set to `false`, CubeVS installs a `0.0.0.0/0` deny-all rule and relies on explicit allow targets to punch holes.

With `allow_internet_access=True` (the default), traffic that does not match the L7 `rules` is still forwarded at L3/L4 by default — it bypasses CubeEgress entirely and never hits the deny logic. The sandbox has full internet egress; the "default-deny" exists only in the user's expectation.

Change this to `allow_internet_access=False`. The LLM host extracted from `rules[].match.sni` / `rules[].match.host` is automatically added as an allow target by CubeVS, so the intended traffic (LLM API) is still permitted while everything else is denied.

The same fix is needed in the documentation code snippet in `docs/guide/integrations/pi-agent.md` line 209 and `docs/zh/guide/integrations/pi-agent.md`.

item.body:
## Summary

Add `.github/workflows/publish-python-sdk.yml` to automate publishing the Python SDK to PyPI.

## Changes from PR #638

- **Trigger**: `v*` → `python-sdk-v*` (dedicated Python SDK version tag, decoupled from repo-level tags)
- **Version validation**: tag version must match `pyproject.toml` version AND `cubesandbox/__init__.py` `__version__` — fails fast if mismatched
- **Change detection**: compares against previous `python-sdk-v*` tag (not `v*`), only publishes when `sdk/python/` has actual changes

## Workflow steps

1. Triggered on `python-sdk-v*` tag push
2. **Strong version check**: extract version from tag, compare with `pyproject.toml` and `__init__.py` — exit 1 on mismatch
3. **Change detection**: diff `sdk/python/` since last `python-sdk-v*` tag — skip if no changes
4. Run tests (pytest)
5. Build package (`python -m build`)
6. Validate (`twine check`)
7. Publish to PyPI

## Required secrets

- `CUBE_PYPI_TOKEN` — PyPI upload token

## Tag convention

Use tags like `python-sdk-v0.3.0` where `0.3.0` matches the version in `pyproject.toml`.

Closes #638

review_comments.body: **Consider OIDC trusted publishing**: Using a long-lived PyPI token creates a permanent credential that, if leaked, allows anyone to publish malicious packages under the project name. PyPI's OIDC trusted publishing eliminates this risk — `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` supports it natively when no `password` is provided. Add `id-token: write` to the job's `permissions` block and remove this line.

+name: Publish Python SDK to PyPI
+
+on:
+  push:
+    tags:
+      - 'python-sdk-v*'
+
+jobs:
+  build-and-publish:
+    name: Build and publish to PyPI
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    permissions:
+      contents: read
+
+    steps:
+      - name: Checkout (full history, blobless)
+        uses: actions/checkout@v4
+        with:
+          fetch-depth: 0
+          filter: 'blob:none'
+
+      - name: Verify tag version matches pyproject.toml and __init__.py
+        id: verify_version
+        working-directory: sdk/python
+        run: |
+          CURRENT_TAG="${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"
+          # Extract version from tag: python-sdk-v0.3.0 -> 0.3.0
+          TAG_VERSION="${CURRENT_TAG#python-sdk-v}"
+          echo "Tag version: $TAG_VERSION"
+
+          # Extract version from pyproject.toml
+          PYPROJECT_VERSION=$(grep -m1 '^version' pyproject.toml | sed 's/version *= *"\(.*\)"/\1/')
+          echo "pyproject.toml version: $PYPROJECT_VERSION"
+
+          # Extract version from __init__.py
+          INIT_VERSION=$(grep -m1 '__version__' cubesandbox/__init__.py | sed 's/.*__version__ *= *"\(.*\)".*/\1/')
+          echo "__init__.py version: $INIT_VERSION"
+
+          if [ "$TAG_VERSION" != "$PYPROJECT_VERSION" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Tag version ($TAG_VERSION) does not match pyproject.toml version ($PYPROJECT_VERSION)"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+
+          if [ "$TAG_VERSION" != "$INIT_VERSION" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Tag version ($TAG_VERSION) does not match __init__.py __version__ ($INIT_VERSION)"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+
+          echo "All versions match: $TAG_VERSION"
+
+      - name: Check if sdk/python/ changed since last tag
+        id: check_changes
+        run: |
+          CURRENT_TAG="${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"
+          echo "Current tag: $CURRENT_TAG"
+
+          PREV_TAG=$(git describe --tags --first-parent --match 'python-sdk-v*' --abbrev=0 "${CURRENT_TAG}^" 2>/dev/null || true)
+
+          if [ -z "$PREV_TAG" ]; then
+            echo "No previous python-sdk tag found -- first release, proceeding."
+            echo "changed=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+          else
+            echo "Comparing $PREV_TAG -> $CURRENT_TAG for sdk/python/ changes"
+            CHANGED=$(git diff --name-only "$PREV_TAG" "$CURRENT_TAG" -- sdk/python/)
+            if [ -n "$CHANGED" ]; then
+              echo "sdk/python/ has changes:"
+              echo "$CHANGED"
+              echo "changed=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+            else
+              echo "No changes in sdk/python/ since $PREV_TAG -- skipping publish."
+              echo "changed=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+            fi
+          fi
+
+      - name: Set up Python

@ls-ggg Thanks for the review!

The main reason we went beyond CLI-only completion is that several API-level
entry points also accept sandbox IDs:

- cubemastercli subcommands (sandbox info, exec, update, setTimeout, refresh)
  call the HTTP API with the raw short ID — CLI completion alone wouldn't help.
- CubeMaster HTTP handlers for snapshot create/rollback, template commit, and
  sandbox logs resolve IDs from request parameters, not CLI input.
- Cubelet's Store.Get() is called internally by the gRPC server and List filter
  pipeline — no CLI in the path at all.

A CLI-only approach would require every API consumer and CLI subcommand to
repeatedly implement the same resolution logic. Sharing a small `sandboxid`
package in both CubeMaster and Cubelet keeps the surface minimal and avoids
duplication.

That said, if you prefer we keep the resolver purely in cubecli for now and
revisit the API-side later, happy to adjust — just wanted to be clear on the
motivation for the current approach.

item.body:
## Summary

Sandbox IDs are 32-character lowercase hex strings (UUID without dashes). `cubecli ls` truncates them to 12 characters for display, but several APIs and CLIs previously required the full ID or used naive `strings.HasPrefix` matching without ambiguity checks.

This PR adds a shared sandbox ID resolver and wires it through CubeMaster, Cubelet, and CLI entry points so that:

- **Display** can stay short (12-char truncation unchanged; `--no-trunc` still shows the full ID)
- **Input** accepts either a full 32-char ID or a **unique** short prefix
- **Ambiguous** prefixes return a clear error instead of silently matching the wrong sandbox
- **Missing** IDs return a not-found error

### Core resolver (`sandboxid.Resolve`)

| Case | Behavior |
|------|----------|
| Exact match (case-insensitive hex) | Return canonical full ID |
| Unique prefix among candidates | Return the matching full ID |
| Multiple prefix matches | `ambiguous sandbox id prefix` |
| No match, input is 32-char hex | Passthrough (downstream validates existence) |
| No match, input is short prefix | `sandbox id not found` |

### Changes by component

**CubeMaster**
- New `pkg/sandboxid/` with table-driven unit tests
- New `ResolveSandboxID()` in `pkg/service/sandbox/`:
  - Resolves against `localcache.ListKnownSandboxIDs()`
  - Falls back to listing sandboxes from healthy Cubelet nodes when cache is cold
- Wired into: `SandboxInfo`, `DestroySandbox`, `Exec`, `Update`, `SetTimeout`, `Refresh`
- HTTP handlers: snapshot create/rollback, template commit, sandbox logs
- `cubemastercli list --sandboxid` filter uses prefix resolution

**Cubelet**
- New `pkg/sandboxid/` (same logic, separate module)
- `pkg/store/cubebox.Store.Get()` resolves short/full IDs before indexer lookup
- `List` filter by `id` benefits automatically via `Get()`

**cubecli**
- `destroy` and `inspect`/`info` (metadata) use resolver instead of raw `HasPrefix`
- Ambiguous or missing prefixes surface as CLI errors

### Out of scope (unchanged)

- `cubecli ls` default 12-char display truncation
- Container ID prefix resolution (containerd `CompleteShortId` path unchanged)
- SDK model changes (no new fields; clients pass short or full ID as before)

## Motivation

Users often copy the truncated ID from `cubecli ls` and then fail on `cubemastercli sandbox info -s <prefix>` or `cubecli destroy <prefix>`. This aligns behavior with the common expectation: **show short, accept short when unique**.

Example:

```bash
# cubecli ls shows: a1b2c3d4e5f6 ...
cubemastercli sandbox info -s a1b2c3d4e5f6   # works when prefix is unique
cubecli destroy a1b2c3d4e5f6                   # works when prefix is unique
cubecli destroy a1b2                          # error if multiple sandboxes share prefix

review_comments.body:
1. **Full-ID passthrough** — removed. `sandboxid.Resolve` now requires an exact or unique-prefix match in candidates; arbitrary 32-char hex strings return `ErrNotFound`. Dropped `tryResolveSandboxID` and the `IsFullID` bypass.

2. **Cluster collect observability** — per-node `cubelet.List` failures are logged at warn level. Goroutines respect `ctx.Done()` and exit early on cancellation.

3. **Collect/cache separation** — `collectClusterSandboxIDs` only gathers entries; `cacheCollectedSandboxEntries` updates `localcache` as an explicit post-step in `ResolveSandboxID`. Concurrent node queries capped at 32 (same fan-out pattern as `ListSandbox`).

4. **`Store.Get()` performance** — full 32-char IDs take an O(1) `getByKey` fast-path; prefix resolution (O(N) store scan) runs only for short inputs.

Unit tests updated: full ID without a matching candidate now expects `ErrNotFound`.

**Store.Get() regression: O(1) → O(N) on every lookup**

`resolveID` calls `s.List()` which returns ALL items from the indexer (iterate + type-assert every object) and then `sandboxid.Resolve` iterates twice more. A single `Get()` now performs ~5 passes over all N items plus 2 full retrievals from the indexer, versus the original single O(1) hash lookup via `indexer.GetByKey`.

`resolveID` is called on every `Get()`, which is invoked from dozens of call sites (destroy, exec, update, snapshot, etc.).

**Fix:** Add a fast-path for full 32-char hex IDs — check `sandboxid.IsFullID(id)` before enumerating the store, and fall through to prefix resolution only when the input is a short prefix. This restores O(1) for the common case (full IDs) and only pays O(N) for short prefix inputs.

**Collect + cache — side-effect coupling violates single responsibility**

This function is named "collect IDs" but also mutates global state (`localcache.SetSandboxCache`). Callers that only want to resolve an ID will incidentally populate the cache. This makes testing harder (cache must be set up or mocked) and makes data flow implicit.

Either:
1. Separate the cache population into a post-processing step called by `ResolveSandboxID` after collection
2. Or rename the function to reflect the side effect (e.g., `collectAndCacheClusterSandboxIDs`)

Also note: there's no rate limiting on the concurrent node queries. `GetHealthyNodes(-1)` could return hundreds of nodes, spawning an equal number of concurrent gRPC calls.

**Silent error swallowing degrades observability**

Errors from individual node queries during cluster-wide sandbox collection are silently discarded. If a node is unreachable or returns an error, the function continues with whatever IDs it collected from other nodes — this partial failure is completely invisible in production logs.

At minimum, log the error here. If many nodes are failing, the operator should know. Also consider that `ctx` cancellation is never checked — if the caller cancels, the goroutines keep running until `wg.Wait()` returns.

**Full-ID passthrough bypasses candidate validation**

When a user supplies a full 32-char hex ID that matches none of the candidates, this returns the input (lowercased) as if it were valid. `tryResolveSandboxID` at `id_resolve.go:45-46` then also accepts it because `IsFullID(resolved)` is true.

This means any arbitrary 32-char hex string resolves successfully through both layers regardless of whether it corresponds to a real sandbox. While the downstream operation (`Destroy`, `Exec`, etc.) may eventually fail when it can't find the sandbox, the error will be misleading because the resolver reported success.

Either:
1. Remove this passthrough (resolve.go:52-53 and the corresponding check at id_resolve.go:45-46), treating full IDs that aren't in the candidate list as "not found"
2. Or make it an explicit opt-in parameter so callers consciously choose this behavior

`resolveID` calls `s.List()` which enumerates ALL items from the indexer (iterate + type-assert every object), then `s.Len()` calls `List()` again just for a capacity hint, then `sandboxid.Resolve` iterates twice more. ## Review: PR #696 -- Expose volume mounts in sandbox info/list APIs

Overall a well-structured, multi-layer change that correctly propagates volume mount data from Cubelet up through CubeMaster and CubeAPI. The test coverage for the new functions is solid, and the code follows established patterns. Below are the findings I consider most noteworthy.

---

### High Severity

**1. hostPath disclosure to all API consumers (Security -- CWE-200)**

The hostPath field of host-directory mounts is exposed to every authenticated caller of GET /sandboxes and GET /sandboxes/{id}, revealing host filesystem layout to tenants that did not create the mount. In a multi-tenant environment this leaks server-side paths.

**Recommendation:** Either redact hostPath from API responses (it is an implementation detail the sandbox consumer does not need), or add authorization so only the sandbox owner can see it.

**2. ContainerInfo.VolumeMounts defined but never populated (Code quality)**

ContainerInfo at types/types.go:513 has a VolumeMounts []*VolumeMountInfo field, but neither doget() (bcakofffice : sandbox_info.go) nor doOneList() (scandbox_list.go) populates it -- volume mounts are only set at the SandboxData level.

**Recommendation:** Either populate containerInfo.VolumeMounts in the loop at sandbox_info.go:158, or remove the field from ContainerInfo.

**3. Rust map_volume_mounts() -- per-call heap allocations scale with list size (Performance)**

map_volume_mounts() is called once per sandbox on every list/info API call. For each mount, every String field is cloned from an already-deserialized CubeVolumeMount into a SandboxVolumeMount.

**Recommendation:** Deserialize directly into SandboxVolumeMount using serde(alias), eliminating the intermediate type.

---

### Medium Severity

**4. Path traversal not blocked in injectHostDirMounts (Security -- CWE-22)**
hostdir_mount.go validates only strings.HasPrefix(o.HostPath, "/") -- a hostPath of /tmp/../../../etc/passwd passes the check.

**Recommendation:** Use filepath.Clean() before the HasPrefix check and consider an allowlist of permitted parent directories.

**5. Volume mount metadata visible across tenants in list API (Security -- CWE-862)**
The list API returns volume mounts for all sandboxes on a node regardless of ownership.

**Recommendation:** Apply label/annotation-based access filtering to volume mount exposure, similar to matchFilter() in sandbox_list.go.

**6. Go double iteration over mounts with intermediate allocation (Performance)**
collectVolumeMountsFromContainers() and volumeMountsToContainerInfo() at volume_mounts.go:19-62 are always called as a pair, creating an intermediate slice.

**Recommendation:** Merge into a single function that filters and converts in one pass.

**7. Shared pointer aliasing in injectHostDirMounts (Code quality)**
The vm slice at hostdir_mount.go:90-97 is appended to every container -- all containers share the same proto struct pointers.

**Recommendation:** Use proto.Clone() or construct fresh structs per container.

**8. No backward-compatibility test for responses without volumeMounts (Test coverage)**
No SDK test asserts that a pre-feature JSON response (without volumeMounts) decodes without error.

**Recommendation:** Add one test per SDK layer serving the old response format.

---

### Low Severity

- OpenAPI SandboxVolumeMount properties lack descriptions (openapi.yml lines 938-952).
- Rust struct and proto fields lack doc comments.
- map_volume_mounts always wraps read_only in Some(bool).
- Missing test cases: injectHostDirMounts with multiple mount options; error path for non-absolute paths; nil mount inside a valid container.

---

### Positive aspects

- Helper functions are clean, single-responsibility, with sensible nil/empty handling.
- Proto field number 10 (next available) avoids wire compatibility issues.
- The sandbox pod container is correctly skipped, preventing internal infrastructure mounts from leaking.
- Go SDK and Python SDK tests validate deserialization end-to-end.
- Rust serde aliases handle Go-side protobuf JSON field naming conventions.

<!-- cubesandbox-auto-review:start -->

## Code review: PR #694 — Claude Code + CubeSandbox integration

Overall impression: a well-structured, comprehensive PR. The code quality is high, the documentation is thorough and consistent across both languages, and the security-sensitive patterns (shlex.quote, credential vault, per-exec env forwarding) are handled correctly. Below are the findings I consider noteworthy after reviewing the reviewer reports.

---

### Noteworthy issues

**1. Sandbox resource leak with `--pause` + early error** (`run_claude.py:179-193`)

When `--pause` is requested but an error occurs before `sandbox.pause()` is reached (e.g., preflight fails), the `finally` block skips cleanup because `not args.pause` is `False`. The sandbox stays alive until timeout. Track whether pause was actually performed rather than guarding on the flag alone.

**2. Non-reproducible Docker builds** (`Dockerfile:25`)

`ARG CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION=latest` means the same `docker build` produces different images over time. A breaking upstream change becomes a silent CI/CD failure. Pin a specific version as the default, and encourage `--build-arg` in README build instructions for production use.

**3. Doc snippet doesn't match version table's `--build-arg` claim** (`docs/guide/integrations/claude-code.md:96-111`)

The version table advertises version pinning via `--build-arg CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION=x.y.z`, but the Dockerfile snippet in the guide hardcodes `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` with no variable. The actual `Dockerfile` does use the `ARG`. Please align the snippet and the table.

**4. `network_policy.py` docstring understates key storage** (`network_policy.py:14-16`)

The docstring says the key "only lives in the operator's rule list", but the rule list (containing the key) is transmitted to and stored by the CubeAPI control plane as part of `Sandbox.create(network={"rules": ...})`. Users should understand this trade-off: the key never enters the VM's process space, but it does pass through the Cube control plane. Consider updating the docstring and README section 5 to state this explicitly.

**5. `CLAUDE_WORKSPACE` and `SSL_CERT_FILE` missing from env var tables**

These variables are documented in `env.example` and consumed by the scripts, but absent from all four env var tables (both READMEs and both integration guides). Either add them to the tables or remove them from `env.example` if they are not intended for end-user documentation.

---

### Minor / optional suggestions

- **No non-root user in Dockerfile** — Claude Code and all spawned processes run as root inside the VM. While KVM isolation prevents host escape, adding a `USER` directive (e.g. a `claude` user) would provide defense-in-depth within the sandbox boundary. Would require adjusting the `user="root"` parameters in the driver scripts.
- **`upload_seed` has no file size limit** (`run_claude.py:100-107`) — Consider adding a size check or using streaming to avoid loading the entire file into memory. Low risk since `--seed` is a developer-facing option.

---

*Review performed by automated reviewer agents (code-quality, security, documentation-accuracy). Findings synthesized and assessed by the lead reviewer.*
<!-- cubesandbox-auto-review:end -->

Thanks for the review — pushed [`9d10891`](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/694/commits/9d10891) addressing all six comments:

| # | Comment | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `--verbose` doesn't mean verbosity, it means stream-json output | Renamed to `--stream-json`; docstring/help/README/guide all updated |
| 2 | `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK` / `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX` silently forwarded but undocumented | Added to env-var tables in both READMEs and both integration guides; `env.example` now lists them with mutual-exclusion note |
| 3 | `resume_claude.py` sandbox leak if `.sandbox_id` access raised | Moved `.sandbox_id` inside the `try`; also propagate accumulated per-turn exit codes |
| 4 | `run_claude()` exit codes swallowed | Now returned + summed; `main()` returns non-zero when any turn failed |
| 5 | `npm install -g` bloat in `/root/.npm` | Added `npm cache clean --force && rm -rf /root/.npm` in the same RUN chain — local rebuild dropped image size from **1.33 GB → 287 MB** |
| 6 | Missing `.gitignore` for `.env` | Added `examples/claude-code-integration/.gitignore` covering `.env`, `__pycache__/`, `*.pyc` |

Local re-verification after the changes:
- `docker build --platform linux/amd64` still succeeds
- envd `/health` inside the running image still returns **204**
- `claude --version` still `2.1.197 (Claude Code)`
- `test -d /root/.npm/_cacache` returns "cache cleaned"
- All four Python scripts still `py_compile`

The end-to-end run against a live cluster + real Anthropic key still needs a maintainer with cluster access, since I don't have one on hand.

Round-2 auto-review surfaced four real bugs in [`9d10891`](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/694/commits/9d10891). Pushed [`a514206`](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/pull/694/commits/a514206) fixing all four:

| # | Bug | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `run_claude.py --pause` was a no-op — `with Sandbox.create()` `__exit__` killed the sandbox immediately after pause | Switched to explicit `try/finally`; only call `sandbox.kill()` when `--pause` is off, so a paused sandbox actually survives the script |
| 2 | `resume_claude.py` `result.exit_code or 0` conflated `None` (SDK error) with `0` (success) | Now returns `1` when `exit_code is None`, otherwise the real code — `failures` counter now increments as intended |
| 3 | `run_claude.py --seed` had no warning that seeded files are readable by the agent (potential exfil path for SSH keys / creds) | Added a WARNING clause to the `--seed` help text |
| 4 | `resume_claude.py` `finally` block would `NameError` on `sandbox.kill()` if `Sandbox.create()` itself raised, silently swallowing the original exception | Moved `Sandbox.create(...)` inside the `try`; `finally` now guards with `if sandbox is not None` |

Verified locally: all four Python scripts still `py_compile` clean. The image build hasn't changed, so the earlier smoke test (envd `/health` = 204, `claude --version` = 2.1.197, cache cleaned, 287 MB) still applies.
Refs #644

Hello, thank you for your contribution! Since we have a large number of participants in this event, to speed up the PR review process, could you please attach some screenshots and logs (both are needed) showing the verification process and results for this PR? Thank you for your participation!

## Summary

Addresses the **Claude Code** sub-direction of #644 with an end-to-end
integration guide plus a runnable example project.

- **Runnable example** at [`examples/claude-code-integration/`](../tree/master/examples/claude-code-integration):

  - `resume_claude.py` — pause/resume across two turns; verifies `/workspace` + `/root/.claude/` survive the snapshot.
  - `network_policy.py` — recommended **credential vault** pattern: default-deny egress, allow only `api.anthropic.com`, CubeEgress `inject` attaches `x-api-key` on the wire so the key never enters the VM.
  - Bilingual `README.md` / `README_zh.md`, `env.example`, `requirements.txt`, `env_utils.py`.
- **Integration guide** in both languages, following the `_template.md` frontmatter and referenced in the index tables:

  - [`docs/zh/guide/integrations/claude-code.md`](../tree/master/docs/zh/guide/integrations/claude-code.md)

Covers the acceptance criteria from #644:
1. end-to-end integration guide (template build, deps, key injection, egress policy, session persistence via snapshots),

@@ -0,0 +1,331 @@
+---
+title: Claude Code Integration Guide
+author: LangQi99
+date: 2026-07-01
+tags:
+  - integration
+  - claude-code
+  - anthropic
+  - agent
+lang: en-US
+---
+
+# Claude Code Integration Guide
+
+[中文文档](../../zh/guide/integrations/claude-code.md)
+
+Run [Anthropic Claude Code](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code) —
+the terminal-native AI coding agent — inside CubeSandbox MicroVMs. This guide
+covers everything from image build to production egress control, and pairs
+with the runnable [`examples/claude-code-integration`](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/tree/master/examples/claude-code-integration)
+project.
+
+## Integration Target and Version
+
+| Component | Version |
+|---|---|
+| Claude Code CLI | `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` (latest at build time; pinned via `--build-arg CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION=x.y.z`) |
+| Node.js | 20 LTS |
+| CubeSandbox base image | `ghcr.io/tencentcloud/cubesandbox-base:2026.16` |
+| E2B SDK (host driver) | `e2b >= 2.4.1` |
+| CubeSandbox platform | `>= 0.3.0` (pause/resume) / `>= 0.4.0` (credential vault via CubeEgress) |
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- CubeSandbox deployment reachable at CubeAPI (`http://<node>:3000`)
+- `cubemastercli` on `$PATH` and connected to the cluster
+- Docker on the workstation used to build the template image, plus a registry
+  the Cube nodes can pull from
+- Anthropic API key (`sk-ant-...`) — or a compatible gateway (Bedrock, Vertex,
+  in-house Anthropic proxy)
+- Python 3.10+ for the host driver scripts
+
+## Why Run Claude Code Inside a Sandbox
+
+Claude Code is a terminal agent that edits files, runs commands, and installs
+packages. Running it directly on your workstation blends the agent's blast
+radius with your dev environment. Running it inside CubeSandbox gives you:
+
+| Concern | CubeSandbox provides |
+|---|---|
+| **Isolation** | KVM MicroVM per session, dedicated guest kernel |
+| **Reproducibility** | Every session boots from the same template snapshot |
+| **Fast spin-up** | Sub-60 ms cold start, so N-parallel agents are cheap |
+| **Long tasks** | `sandbox.pause()` snapshots VM + rootfs; resume later |
+| **Key hygiene** | CubeEgress injects `x-api-key` on the wire — the VM never sees it |
+| **Egress audit** | Every request to `api.anthropic.com` lands in a JSONL audit log |
+
+## Architecture
+
+```
+┌────────────────────────┐        ┌───────────────────────┐
+│  Host driver script     │  E2B  │  CubeSandbox MicroVM  │
+│  (run_claude.py)        │       │                       │
+│                         │──────►│  envd (:49983)        │
+│  ANTHROPIC_API_KEY      │       │  claude CLI (Node 20) │
+│  optional               │       │  git / python / rg    │
+│                         │       │  /workspace           │
+└──────────┬──────────────┘       └───────────┬───────────┘
+           │                                  │ HTTPS
+           │                                  ▼
+           │                           ┌───────────────┐
+           └── inject rule ──────────► │  CubeEgress   │───► api.anthropic.com
+                                       └───────────────┘
+                                              │
+                                              ▼
+                                  /data/log/cube-egress/access.jsonl
+```
+
+Two integration flavors are supported and interchangeable at the SDK level:
+
+| Flavor | Key flow | Best for |
+|---|---|---|
+| **Direct** | `envs={"ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": key}` per exec call | Single-tenant dev machines, quick trials |
+| **Vault** | `Sandbox.create(network={"rules": [inject rule]})` | Shared clusters, hosted services, audit-heavy environments |
+
+Both flavors share the same template — the only difference is whether the key
+is forwarded into the sandbox or attached in-flight by CubeEgress.
+
+## Integration Steps
+
+### 1. Build the template image
+
+The image stacks Node.js 20 and Anthropic's official CLI on top of
+`cubesandbox-base`, so envd is already listening on `:49983`.
+
+```dockerfile
+# examples/claude-code-integration/Dockerfile
+FROM ghcr.io/tencentcloud/cubesandbox-base:2026.16
+
+RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
+      ca-certificates curl gnupg git jq ripgrep less \
+      python3 python3-pip build-essential \
+    && curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_20.x | bash - \
+    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends nodejs \
+    && npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code \
+    && claude --version
+
+ENV CLAUDE_CODE_HOME=/root/.claude
+WORKDIR /workspace
+EXPOSE 49983

**Resource leak: sandbox not killed when `--pause` is combined with an early error.**  

If a user passes `--pause` but `preflight_agent()` fails (or any error occurs before `sandbox.pause()` is reached), the `finally` block skips cleanup because `not args.pause` is still `False`. The sandbox remains alive until its timeout expires, wasting cluster resources.

Consider tracking whether the pause was actually performed:

```python
paused = False
try:
    ...
    if args.pause:
        info = sandbox.pause()
        paused = True
        ...
finally:
    if not paused:
        sandbox.kill()
```

**Bug: `--pause` flag is defeated by the context manager**

When `--pause` is used, the sandbox is paused on line 171, but then the `with` block exits, and the context manager's `__exit__` almost certainly calls `kill()` — destroying the just-paused sandbox. The `--pause` flag is effectively a no-op.

Compare with `resume_claude.py`, which correctly manages the sandbox lifecycle via `try/finally` (no context manager) precisely so the sandbox can outlive the lexical scope.

**Recommendation:** Either remove the `--pause` flag, or manage the sandbox lifecycle manually (like `resume_claude.py`) when pause is active:

```python
sandbox = Sandbox.create(template=template_id, timeout=args.timeout)
try:
    ...
    if args.pause:
        sandbox.pause()
finally:
    if not args.pause:
        sandbox.kill()
```

item.body:
# PR: Fix MySQL 1213 Deadlock in Concurrent Snapshot Rollback

## Problem

During concurrent stress testing with `bench_rollback_concurrency.py -c 5 -n 5`, CubeMaster consistently returns `Error 1213 (40001): Deadlock found when trying to get lock; try restarting transaction`.

### Root Cause

`AcquireSnapshotRuntimeRef` in `CubeMaster/pkg/templatecenter/snapshot_runtime_ref.go` uses a **single database transaction** to handle both "current ACTIVE state" and "RELEASED history", with the following pattern:

```go
// Within a transaction:
// 1. UPDATE ... WHERE sandbox_id = ? AND status = 'ACTIVE' SET status = 'RELEASED'
// 2. INSERT ... (... status = 'ACTIVE' ...)
```

During concurrent rollbacks, multiple transactions with different sandbox IDs enter this path simultaneously. When the corresponding sandbox **has no prior ACTIVE record**, step 1 is a no-match UPDATE. Under InnoDB's default `REPEATABLE READ` isolation level, a no-match UPDATE with a secondary index range condition acquires **gap/next-key locks**. Multiple transactions each hold gap locks on the `(sandbox_id, status)` secondary index, then attempt to INSERT new ACTIVE rows (requiring insert intention locks), forming a **circular wait** on the same index range and triggering the 1213 deadlock.

### Why Simple Retry Is Not Enough

This data model has three fundamental problems:

1. **The deadlock is rooted in the data model**: `t_cube_snapshot_runtime_ref` is overloaded as both a state table and a history table, using `UPDATE status` + `INSERT ACTIVE` to simulate state transitions. InnoDB gap locks are unavoidable with this pattern.
2. **TOCTOU / double ACTIVE**: Changing to "SELECT first, then INSERT" without a DB-level unique constraint would allow concurrent inserts for the same sandbox, producing double ACTIVE records.
3. **Cross-instance safety**: In-process `withTemplateWriteLock` only protects a single CubeMaster instance, not multi-instance deployments.

Merely adding MySQL 1213 retries or application-level locks can reduce failures but cannot fix the root cause.

## Design

### Core Idea: Separating Concerns

Split the original single table's dual responsibilities into two dedicated tables:

- **`t_cube_snapshot_runtime_active`** (new): The authoritative current binding state table for all read paths. Its primary key `(sandbox_id, binding_type)` guarantees at most one current binding per sandbox, and `INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE` provides InnoDB row locks as the concurrency control point.
- **`t_cube_snapshot_runtime_ref`** (retained): Degraded to an audit/history log, INSERT-only. No more `WHERE status='ACTIVE'` range UPDATEs on the hot path.

```
Rollback/Create success ──→ SnapshotRuntimeBindingService ──→ t_cube_snapshot_runtime_active (current state)
Destroy hook ─────────────→                                  ──→ t_cube_snapshot_runtime_ref   (history/audit)
Reconciler ───────────────→
```

### Key Changes

#### 1. New active binding table (migration)

```sql
CREATE TABLE t_cube_snapshot_runtime_active (
  sandbox_id   VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL,
  binding_type VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'memory_backing',
  snapshot_id  VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL,
  node_id      VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  node_ip      VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  memory_vol   VARCHAR(256) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  rootfs_vol   VARCHAR(256) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  sandbox_gen  INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  attached_at  DATETIME     NOT NULL,
  last_seen_at DATETIME     DEFAULT NULL,
  last_error   TEXT,
  created_at   DATETIME     NOT NULL,
  updated_at   DATETIME     NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (sandbox_id, binding_type),
  KEY idx_snapshot_runtime_active_snapshot (snapshot_id),
  KEY idx_snapshot_runtime_active_node (node_id)
) ENGINE=InnoDB;
```

Migration steps:
- Normalize empty `binding_type` in old table ACTIVE rows to `memory_backing`
- For multiple ACTIVE records with the same `(sandbox_id, binding_type)`, keep the one with the largest `id` (consistent with existing `ORDER BY id DESC` behavior)
- Backfill deduplicated ACTIVE rows into the new active table

#### 2. Unified write entry point (`snapshot_runtime_ref.go`)

- **`AttachSnapshotRuntimeBinding(ctx, ref, reason)`**: Called after rollback/create success. Uses `clause.OnConflict` to generate `INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE`, with the primary key `(sandbox_id, binding_type)` as the concurrency control point. Serialized by InnoDB row locks even across multiple CubeMaster instances.
- **`DetachSnapshotRuntimeBinding(ctx, sandboxID, bindingType, reason)`**: Called by destroy hook or when the reconciler no longer observes a sandbox. Executes a DELETE on the active table.
- **`RefreshSnapshotRuntimeBindingsFromNode(ctx, nodeID, nodeIP, observed)`**: Called by the reconciler, internally reuses attach/detach semantics.
- Legacy `AcquireSnapshotRuntimeRef` / `ReleaseSnapshotRuntimeRefsBySandbox` retained as compatibility entry points, delegating to the new implementation.

#### 3. Read path migration

The following functions are switched from reading the old table with `WHERE status='ACTIVE'` to reading the active table, no longer relying on `ORDER BY id DESC` to tolerate dirty data:

- `ListActiveSnapshotRuntimeRefs`
- `GetActiveSnapshotRuntimeRefBySandbox`
- `CountActiveSnapshotRuntimeRefs`
- `populateSnapshotRuntimeRefSummary`
- Active ref check in `DeleteSnapshot`
- `allocateNextRollbackGen`

#### 4. Snapshot operation lock hardening (`snapshot_ops.go`)

Multi-level distributed locks introduced for snapshot create and rollback operations:

- `snapshot-sandbox:<sandboxID>`: sandbox-level mutual exclusion
- `snapshot-resource:<snapshotID>`: snapshot resource-level mutual exclusion
- `snapshot-request:<requestID>`: request idempotency guarantee

`withSnapshotWriteLocks` recursively acquires multiple locks, ensuring that only one snapshot-related write operation enters for a given sandbox at a time.

#### 5. Error classification fix

Fixed the database error mapping in `snapshotErrorCode()`. Database errors are no longer misreported as `MasterParamsError(130400)` and are now correctly mapped to `DBError`.

#### 6. New constant

- `SnapshotRuntimeActiveTableName = "t_cube_snapshot_runtime_active"`

## Why Other Approaches Were Rejected

| Approach | Problem |
|----------|---------|
| "SELECT id first, then UPDATE by primary key" only | TOCTOU under concurrent writes to the same sandbox, double ACTIVE possible |
| `withTemplateWriteLock` process lock only | Only protects a single instance, not multi-instance deployments |
| MySQL 1213 retry only | Reduces failure rate but does not fix the data model |
| Partial unique constraint on old table | Cannot use generated columns (no precedent in repo), still retains mixed responsibilities and history growth issues |

## Verification

- [x] Concurrent attach to same sandbox: active table has exactly one row, final value matches the last successful write
- [x] Concurrent attach to different sandboxes: no deadlocks
- [x] Interleaved rollback attach + destroy detach + reconciler refresh: no double bindings
- [x] Snapshot view / delete precheck returns consistent results from active table
- [x] Snapshot delete returns conflict when active consumers exist
- [x] Database errors mapped to `DBError`, no longer misreported as `MasterParamsError(130400)`
- [x] Stress test `bench_rollback_concurrency.py -c 5 -n 20` and `-c 10`: no 1213 deadlocks
- [x] `SHOW ENGINE INNODB STATUS`: no runtime ref related deadlocks

## Risk Control

- Migration retains the old table, no historical data is destroyed
- All writers converge on `SnapshotRuntimeBindingService`, preventing multiple entry points from maintaining state independently
- The active table primary key `(sandbox_id, binding_type)` is the root of concurrency correctness; no reliance on application-level locks
- Cubelet rollback execution semantics are unchanged; only the metadata model is modified

item.body:
## Motivation

An unhealthy host mount, such as a geesefs path with revoked remote access, can block the Cubelet hostdir bind step indefinitely. When that happens, sandbox creation hangs until an upstream API timeout even though the real failure is already at the hostdir mount boundary.

Cubelet should fail fast when a hostdir bind cannot complete, instead of leaving the create path blocked by a hung mount operation.

## What Changed

This PR makes Cubelet hostdir mounts fail fast by moving the bind operation out of the create goroutine and into a bounded helper subprocess.

Implementation highlights:

* `Cubelet/storage/hostdir.go` replaces the in-process `unix.Mount(...)` hostdir bind with `mount --rbind` executed through a helper subprocess
* each hostdir mount step is bounded to 3s
* read-only hostdir mounts keep the follow-up `remount,bind,ro` step under the same bounded helper path
* hostdir backend metadata is recorded before the bind attempt so cleanup still knows the sandbox-scoped hostdir paths after a failed create
* the top-level error category stays `CreateStorageFailed`, while the returned message now makes the hostdir timeout explicit
* `Cubelet/storage/hostdir_test.go` adds focused coverage for command shape, timeout/error handling, and real subprocess timeout cleanup

The timeout is per mount step rather than a flat per-request cap:

* read-write hostdir: up to about 3s per volume
* read-only hostdir: up to about 6s per volume, because bind and remount are bounded separately

## Testing

Focused unit tests:

```bash
go test ./storage -run HostDir -count=1
```

Covered cases:

* read-write hostdir helper command shape
* read-only hostdir bind + remount helper command shape
* timeout handling
* generic mount-error handling
* real subprocess timeout behavior, including prompt return and child process-group cleanup

Real-cluster healthy-path validation:

* with a healthy host mount, sandbox creation still succeeded in about `0.108s`

Real-cluster failure-path validation:

* reproduced an unhealthy geesefs-backed host mount where `ls` on the host path blocked indefinitely
* before this fix, sandbox creation hung until the upstream API timeout
* after this fix, CubeAPI returned `500 Internal Server Error` in about `3010ms`
* Cubelet returned `CreateStorageFailed` with a hostdir-specific timeout message, for example:

```text
prepareHostDirVolume: bind mount /mnt/aime-oss/test -> /data/cubelet/hostdir/<sandbox-id>/rw/hostdir-0 timed out after 3s: context deadline exceeded
```

* CubeMaster propagated the same `CreateStorageFailed` message in `CreateSandbox_rsp fail`
* post-failure checks showed no surviving sandbox in `cubecli cubebox list`
* post-failure checks showed no leftover sandbox hostdir root under `/data/cubelet/hostdir/<sandbox-id>`

Behavioral clarification:

* failure logs may still show a `sandboxID`, `sandboxIP`, and `port_mappings`
* this is expected because `createid` runs before storage, and storage/network run before the final `cubebox` step
* in the reproduced failure, the actual cubebox VM was not created

## Scope

This PR only changes Cubelet hostdir mount failure handling.

Thanks. I looked at the helpers in `storage/shell.go` / `utils.Exec*`.

I kept a dedicated helper here because this path needs one extra guarantee for the stuck-mount case: on timeout, it explicitly kills the whole process group with `Kill(-pid, SIGKILL)`, rather than only relying on the default `exec.CommandContext` cancellation behavior.

The local runner also keeps the timeout / cancel / remount-failure paths directly injectable in unit tests. So I think a small dedicated helper is safer for this hostdir mount path.

review_comments.body: **Test quality: Fragile error assertions** — These tests check only `strings.Contains(err.Error(), "timed out")` rather than also verifying with `errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded)`. The real-subprocess test (`TestDefaultRunHostDirCommandTimeoutKillsProcessGroup`) correctly uses `errors.Is`. Prefer following the same pattern here for robustness against error message rewording. The same applies to the Canceled and MountError tests below.

**Documentation: Missing doc comment** — This function creates two derived contexts with separate timeouts and short-circuits early for `!readOnly`. A brief comment would clarify the context lifecycle for maintainers.

**Documentation: Missing doc comment** — This function uses three non-obvious patterns: (1) `Setpgid: true` to isolate the process group, (2) goroutine + buffered channel for non-blocking `Wait()`, and (3) `syscall.Kill(-pid, SIGKILL)` to kill the entire process group on timeout. A brief doc comment would help future maintainers understand the lifecycle.

**Performance: Read-only timeout stacking** — For read-only volumes, this creates two independent bounded subprocesses (bind at 3s, remount at another 3s), for a worst-case 6s per RO volume. The remount is a pure VFS flag change — it cannot hang independently of the already-succeeded bind. Consider a shorter remount-specific timeout (e.g., 1s) to bound the total wait per volume to ~4s rather than ~6s.

**Security: Unvalidated `host_path`** — `src.GetHostPath()` comes from the API request and flows directly into `mount --rbind` with only an empty-string check. This could allow mounting sensitive host paths (e.g., `/etc`, `/var/lib/kubelet`) into the sandbox.

The codebase already has `pathutil.ValidatePathUnderBase` and `filepath.IsAbs` for this purpose. Please validate the host path before passing it to `bindHostDir`.

**Potential goroutine leak on D-state mount** — If `cmd.Wait()` blocks on a process stuck in uninterruptible sleep (D state, common for NFS-backed mounts), this goroutine leaks permanently since nothing bounds `cmd.Wait()`. Meanwhile, the `ctx.Done()` path already returned. While `done` is buffered (capacity 1), the goroutine still leaks its stack and references. Consider adding a separate goroutine monitoring channel to detect when `cmd.Wait()` has been blocked for a second round of timeout.

**`mount` binary resolved via `$PATH`** — `exec.Command("mount", ...)` relies on `exec.LookPath("mount")`, searching the process's `$PATH`. A manipulated PATH (e.g., world-writable dir before system paths) could let a local attacker with filesystem write supply a malicious `mount` binary. Since `mount --rbind` requires `CAP_SYS_ADMIN`, the subprocess runs with elevated privileges. Use an absolute path like `/usr/bin/mount` (consistent with `/usr/bin/bash` used in `shell.go`).

**No input validation on command name/args** — `exec.Command` passes `name` / `args` directly. While shell metacharacter injection is not possible here (Go's `exec.Command` does not invoke a shell), NUL bytes embedded in protobuf-originating paths like `src.GetHostPath()` would cause a panic (`syscall.BytePtrFromString` fails on embedded NUL). Consider adding validation before the exec call (the codebase has `validateExecArgs` in `shell.go`). Alternatively, use `unix.Mount` with a racy-fd helper for the timeout instead of subprocess — but if keeping the subprocess approach, validate args first.

**Potential goroutine leak on D-state mount** — If `cmd.Wait()` blocks on a process stuck in uninterruptible sleep (D state, common for network-backed mounts), this goroutine leaks permanently since nothing bounds `cmd.Wait()`. The `ctx.Done()` path has already returned by this point. While `done` is buffered (capacity 1), the goroutine still leaks its stack, references, and the `bytes.Buffer` backing `stderr`. Consider adding a second-stage watchdog so that if `cmd.Wait()` hasn't returned within some additional window after the initial timeout, at minimum the stall is logged.

**`mount` binary resolved via `$PATH`** — `exec.Command("mount", ...)` relies on `exec.LookPath("mount")`, searching the process's `$PATH`. A manipulated PATH (e.g., world-writable dir before system paths) could let a local attacker with filesystem write supply a malicious `mount` binary. Since `mount --rbind` requires `CAP_SYS_ADMIN`, the subprocess runs with elevated privileges. Use an absolute path like `/usr/bin/mount` (consistent with `/usr/bin/bash` used in `shell.go`).

**No input validation on command name/args** — `exec.Command` passes `name` / `args` directly. While shell metacharacter injection is not possible here (Go's `exec.Command` does not invoke a shell), NUL bytes embedded in protobuf-originating paths like `src.GetHostPath()` would cause a panic (`syscall.BytePtrFromString` fails on embedded NUL). Consider adding validation before the exec call (the codebase has `validateExecArgs` in `shell.go`). Alternatively, keep at minimum a NUL-byte guard on paths from protobuf fields.

**Metadata recorded before mount succeeds** — `HostDirBackendInfos[key]` is written on line 142, but `bindHostDir` (which can fail) is called on line 151. If the mount fails for volume source 2 of 3, the result already contains metadata for source 1 (and for source 2's metadata itself). While `cleanupHostDirVolumes` happens to be robust enough to handle this gracefully (it walks the directory tree rather than relying on metadata), the semantic gap could confuse callers that inspect `HostDirBackendInfos` after an error. Consider moving the map write to after the mount succeeds, or document why the pre-recording is deliberate.

**`context.Canceled` mislabeled as timeout** — Line 79 checks for both `DeadlineExceeded` and `Canceled`, but the error message says "timed out after 3s" in both cases. If the parent context is canceled (not timed out), the message is misleading. Since the error is returned to the caller, consider distinguishing the two: `"bind mount ... canceled: %w"` for `Canceled`, or at minimum drop `Canceled` from this condition and let it fall through to the generic error wrapping on line 82.

## Notes For Maintainers / Follow-ups

This first version intentionally keeps the implementation focused on CubeAPI lifecycle webhook delivery through `CUBE_API_WEBHOOKS`.

Maintainer confirmation:

- Current defaults are `timeout_secs=3`, `max_retries=3`, with an initial exponential backoff of `200ms`. Please confirm whether these defaults are appropriate for production workloads.
- `sandbox.resumed` is emitted for the explicit `/sandboxes/{sandboxID}/resume` API. Please confirm whether `/sandboxes/{sandboxID}/connect`, when it auto-resumes a paused sandbox, should emit the same event.
- Webhook configuration is environment-based only. API-managed or persisted webhook registry support is not included in this first version.
- `flush()` drains the internal dispatch queue without waiting for all spawned HTTP delivery tasks. This keeps shutdown best-effort and avoids blocking on unreachable receivers; please confirm whether bounded shutdown waiting is desired.

Possible follow-up hardening:

- Define lifecycle event names in a shared code-maintained enum/whitelist so handler emission and subscription validation cannot drift.
- Use bounded delivery queues and fixed workers, potentially with per-endpoint isolation.
- Add a stable `event_id` for receiver-side retry deduplication.
- Add bounded graceful-shutdown waiting plus dropped/failed delivery metrics if the project adopts a metrics path.
- Validate endpoint URLs at startup, limiting them to HTTP(S) while avoiding credential/path/query leakage in logs.

review_comments.body:
**Key name change will force-recreate on existing deployments**

Changing from `cubesandbox_demo_` to `cube_cluster_` prefix means the next `terraform apply` against an existing deployment will attempt to destroy the old key pair and create a new one. Since `tencentcloud_key_pair` lacks `create_before_destroy`, this may fail with "key pair in use" errors on a live cluster where CVMs reference the old key.

Suggestion: consider adding `lifecycle { create_before_destroy = true }` to this resource to mitigate the replacement risk.

**Bash 3.2 array expansion: `${arr[@]:-}` should be `${arr[@]+"${arr[@]}"}`**

On bash 3.2, `${array[@]:-default}` produces one positional argument (the empty string) when the array is empty, instead of zero arguments. This means `ss_print_group` receives one empty detail line and reports a count of 1 for categories with zero resources.

The correct bash 3.2-compatible pattern for safe empty array expansion is `${arr[@]+"${arr[@]}"}` (used correctly earlier in this same file at lines 541-542 and 558-559).

Affected lines: 565, 568, 569, 571, 574, 576.

Minimal diff:
```
-       ss_print_group "${CYAN:-}" "Tracked in state ..." "•" "${sat[@]}"
+       ss_print_group "${CYAN:-}" "Tracked in state ..." "•" "${sat[@]+"${sat[@]}"}"
```

**Minor: `_release_platform` comment overstates jq usage**

The function returns `darwin` for macOS, but jq GitHub release artifacts use `macos` (not `darwin`). The code in `ensure_jq` (line ~305) correctly maps `darwin→macos`, but the header comment suggests the output is directly usable by jq when it is not. Consider clarifying: "OS slug used by HashiCorp release artifacts (linux|darwin). Note: jq releases use 'macos' instead of 'darwin' — see ensure_jq for the mapping."

review_comments.body:
**`TENCENTCLOUD_ENABLE_PUBLIC_NETWORK` has no effect — false sense of security**

`TF_VAR_enable_public_network` is exported here, but `variables.tf` has no `variable "enable_public_network"` and no `.tf` file references it. The `tke-addons.tf` services (cube-api, cube-proxy, cube-webui) always create **internet-facing** LoadBalancer services with `0.0.0.0/0` ingress — the variable never influences whether they're internal or public.

This creates a dangerous false sense of security: the interactive prompt presents the default as "VPC-internal CLBs, reachable only via the jumpserver/VPN" (line ~1635), but that statement is untrue — the services are always exposed to the internet.

Either: (a) wire `var.enable_public_network` into the Terraform services to conditionally set the `internal-subnetid` annotation, or (b) remove this variable entirely and correct the prompt/hardening documentation to honestly state the services are always internet-facing.

<!-- cubesandbox-auto-review:start -->
## Code Review: PR #687 — Webhook Lifecycle Event Delivery

Overall, the PR is well-structured and well-tested. The architecture (async channel-based delivery, per-endpoint filtering, HMAC signing, exponential backoff) is sound. Below are the noteworthy findings organized by priority.

---

### 🔴 High Severity

**1. SSRF risk — webhook endpoint URL is not validated**
`CubeAPI/src/config/mod.rs:297`, `CubeAPI/src/logging/http.rs:124`

The endpoint URL is accepted as-is with only a non-empty check. The `reqwest::Client` has default redirect-following. An attacker controlling the webhook config can point the URL to internal services (cloud metadata endpoints, loopback) — creating an SSRF vector.

**Fix:** Add URL validation (scheme, host/network validation) and set `.redirect(reqwest::redirect::Policy::none())` on the client builder.

---

### 🟠 Medium Severity

**2. Unbounded channel has no backpressure — OOM risk**
`CubeAPI/src/logging/http.rs:122`

`mpsc::unbounded_channel` provides zero backpressure when endpoints are slow. The `JoinHandle` from `tokio::spawn` is also discarded, so the final flush may never execute before runtime teardown.

**Fix:** Use `mpsc::channel(10_000)` and store the `JoinHandle` for shutdown coordination.

**3. Request timeout silently dropped on client builder fallback**
`CubeAPI/src/logging/http.rs:124-134`

When `Client::builder().build()` fails, the fallback `Client::new()` has no configured timeout. A hanging receiver stalls the delivery loop.

**Fix:** Set an explicit `.timeout(...)` on each individual request in `send_with_retries`.

**4. `apply_patch` silently replaces file endpoints**
`CubeAPI/src/config/mod.rs:209-215`

Setting `CUBE_API_WEBHOOK_URL` or `--webhook-url` replaces all file-configured endpoints with a single endpoint. No warning is emitted.

**Fix:** Log a warning when endpoint replacement occurs.

**5. Sidebar removals appear accidental**
`docs/.vitepress/config.mjs`

The sidebar update removed "Snapshot, Rollback & Clone", "Network Policy", "Restrict Public Access", and "Network Hardening".

---

### 🟢 Low Severity

**6. Duplicate `sandbox.resumed` row in events table** (`docs/guide/webhook-events.md:153`)
**7. `http` module still marked as "Stub"** (`CubeAPI/src/logging/mod.rs:23`)
**8. HMAC secret visible via CLI `ps aux`** (`CubeAPI/src/main.rs:139-140`)

---

### ✅ Positive Observations

- Thorough test coverage: pattern matching, HMAC, retry logic, endpoint isolation
- `event_matches_pattern` correctly guards against false prefix matches by checking the separator byte
- Dual-layer event filtering (pre-enqueue and pre-send) provides defence in depth
- Documentation is comprehensive and bilingual

item.body:
Refs #642

Part of the 2026 Tencent Rhino-Bird Open Source Program (2026 犀牛鸟开源项目).

## Motivation

CubeSandbox is used as a sandbox service for AI Agent workloads. Sandboxes may be created, paused, resumed, and deleted frequently, but external systems previously had to poll CubeAPI to observe lifecycle changes.

Issue #642 asks for a webhook event notification mechanism so CubeAPI can push sandbox lifecycle events to external HTTP receivers. The first step needs to provide a reliable delivery foundation: async delivery, endpoint filtering, signing, retry behavior, configuration, tests, an example receiver, and user-facing documentation.

This PR implements that foundation. It intentionally keeps the scope focused to keep the change atomic and reviewable, instead of trying to include every possible webhook-related feature in a single PR.

## What Changed

This PR adds CubeAPI webhook delivery for sandbox lifecycle events.

Specifically, it implements:

* an HTTP webhook backend in `CubeAPI/src/logging/http.rs`
* asynchronous delivery through a background Tokio task
* an internal queue so webhook delivery does not block API handlers
* batched delivery controlled by `batch_size` and `flush_interval_secs`
* multiple webhook endpoints
* endpoint-level event filtering
* exact event matching, for example `sandbox.created`
* prefix wildcard matching, for example `sandbox.*`
* full wildcard matching with `*`
* HMAC-SHA256 request signing through `X-Cube-Webhook-Signature`
* finite retry with exponential backoff
* endpoint isolation, so one failing endpoint does not block other endpoints
* default filtering that avoids sending `api.request` debug noise unless `*` is explicitly subscribed
* lifecycle-aware: master's kill path, `set_timeout`/`refresh` handlers already emit webhook events through the same pipeline

The initial supported lifecycle events are:

* `sandbox.created`
* `sandbox.timeout.updated`
* `sandbox.refreshed`
* `sandbox.paused`
* `sandbox.resumed`
* `sandbox.deleted`

## Configuration

Webhook configuration is wired into CubeAPI startup.

This PR supports three configuration paths:

* config file: supports multiple endpoints
* environment variables: single endpoint, suitable for systemd / one-click deployments
* CLI flags: single endpoint, suitable for local smoke testing

Configuration priority is:

```text
CLI flags > environment variables > config file > defaults
```

## Example Receiver

This PR adds `examples/webhook-receiver/`.

The example receiver is intentionally minimal:

* Python standard library only
* no third-party dependencies
* `POST /webhook` for CubeAPI callbacks
* `GET /health` for connectivity checks
* optional HMAC verification through `WEBHOOK_SECRET`
* English and Chinese README files

The goal is to let users quickly verify webhook delivery locally and reuse the receiver as a reference implementation.

## Documentation

This PR adds VitePress guide pages:

* `docs/guide/webhook-events.md`
* `docs/zh/guide/webhook-events.md`

The guide covers:

* quick start with the example receiver
* supported events
* event subscription patterns
* configuration methods
* payload format and headers
* HMAC-SHA256 signature verification
* retry behavior
* WeCom adapter guidance
* troubleshooting

It also updates the docs sidebar to include the new Webhook Events page.

## Validation

End-to-end validation was completed on a real CubeSandbox systemd / one-click deployment.

Validated behavior:

* example receiver starts successfully
* local curl payload is received by the receiver
* CubeAPI starts with webhook enabled
* `sandbox.created` is delivered after sandbox creation
* `sandbox.timeout.updated` is delivered after `POST /sandboxes/:id/timeout`
* `sandbox.refreshed` is delivered after `POST /sandboxes/:id/refreshes`
* `sandbox.paused` is delivered after sandbox pause
* `sandbox.resumed` is delivered after sandbox resume
* `sandbox.deleted` is delivered after sandbox deletion (via explicit `DELETE` or `kill_sandbox` handler)
* receiver outage does not block sandbox API requests
* valid HMAC signature is accepted
* invalid HMAC signature is rejected
* `api.request` debug events are not delivered by default
* invalid endpoint URL does not block CubeAPI startup or API handlers

Test commands:

```bash
cargo test
cargo test logging::http
cargo check --bin cube-api
```

## Scope

This PR focuses on the core webhook delivery foundation requested by #642.

It does not change the public sandbox API behavior, except for emitting lifecycle events after successful operations. It does not introduce per-request callback URLs, third-party message formatting inside CubeAPI, persistent delivery queues, or new event families beyond the  sandbox lifecycle events.

Follow-up work can build on this foundation:

* Failure-path events: emit events such as `sandbox.create.failed`, `sandbox.pause.failed`, `sandbox.resume.failed`, and `sandbox.delete.failed`, with structured error fields.
* Template and snapshot events: extend the event model to cover template creation/build progress and snapshot lifecycle events.
* Per-request callbacks: allow long-running operations such as template creation or template build to accept a request-scoped `callback_url`, so callers can receive progress updates without polling or watching. This should be designed separately because it needs callback URL validation, SSRF protection, operation correlation, and its own retry semantics.
* Third-party adapters: provide adapter examples for WeCom or generic HTTP alerting endpoints. WeCom bots require `msgtype` + `text` / `markdown` payloads, so CubeAPI should keep emitting a stable JSON event payload and let adapters handle third-party formatting.
* Delivery reliability and observability: add bounded channel backpressure, endpoint circuit breaking, delivery failure counters, latency metrics, dropped-batch metrics, alert hooks, or dead-letter handling if stronger delivery guarantees are needed.
* Unified URL validation policy: if CubeAPI later adopts shared validation for operator-provided URLs, webhook endpoints should follow the same policy.

## Changed Files

Main changed areas:

* `CubeAPI/src/logging/http.rs`
* `CubeAPI/src/logging/multi.rs`
* `CubeAPI/src/config/mod.rs`
* `CubeAPI/src/main.rs`
* `CubeAPI/src/handlers/agenthub.rs`
* `docs/.vitepress/config.mjs`
* `docs/guide/webhook-events.md`
* `docs/zh/guide/webhook-events.md`
* `examples/webhook-receiver/README.md`
* `examples/webhook-receiver/README_zh.md`
* `examples/webhook-receiver/receiver.py`

review_comments.body:
**Request timeout is silently dropped on client builder fallback**

When `reqwest::Client::builder().build()` fails (rare, e.g., TLS backend issue), the fallback `reqwest::Client::new()` has **neither** the configured `timeout()` nor the custom `user_agent`. This means:
- Per-request timeout reverts to reqwest's default (effectively no timeout)
- A hanging webhook receiver can stall the delivery loop indefinitely
- All endpoint processing is blocked (endpoints are iterated sequentially in `flush_buffer`)

**Suggestion:** Either fail fast (`.expect(...)`) on builder failure, or set an explicit `request.timeout(...)` on each individual request in `send_with_retries` as a defence-in-depth measure.

**Unbounded channel has no backpressure — risk of OOM under delivery failures**

`mpsc::unbounded_channel` provides zero backpressure. When endpoints are slow or unreachable, the delivery loop stalls on retry sleeps while `log()` keeps accepting events. The channel grows without bound until memory is exhausted.

Since `flush_buffer` processes endpoints *sequentially* (line 221: `for endpoint in endpoints`), a single slow endpoint blocks delivery to all others, compounding the problem.

**Suggestion:** Replace with a bounded channel (`mpsc::channel(10_000)`) and drop events when full with a warning. Also store the `JoinHandle` from `tokio::spawn` to enable graceful shutdown coordination — currently the handle is discarded, so the `else => break` path that flushes remaining events may never execute before the runtime is dropped.
Acknowledged. Deferring to a follow-up PR alongside circuit breaker.
CubeAPI currently trusts operator-provided URLs across all config fields (AUTH_CALLBACK_URL, DATABASE_URL, etc.). Will revisit if the project adopts a unified URL validation policy.
Acknowledged. Will address in a follow-up performance PR.

**Duplicate default values across config and runtime layers** (Low)

`WebhookConfig` (config/mod.rs:156-169) and `HttpLoggerConfig` (http.rs:73-99) define identical default values independently with different function names. A maintainer changing one default may not remember to update the other.

Consider extracting shared defaults into named constants in a common location (e.g., `logging/mod.rs` or `config/mod.rs`).

**O(E×B) per-endpoint event clones on every flush** (Low)

For each endpoint, all matching events are `.cloned()` into a new `Vec`. With 10 endpoints and 100 events, this is 1000 clones per flush cycle. Each clone bumps `Arc` refcounts and copies owned strings.

Consider a single-pass partitioning into per-endpoint buckets to reduce from O(E×B) to O(B×avg_matches), or reference-counted event ownership to make clones cheap.

**Unbounded channel with no backpressure** (Medium)

`mpsc::unbounded_channel` means the buffer grows without bound when the delivery task can't keep up (e.g., a slow/failing endpoint during retry backoff). Under sustained load this can lead to OOM.

Consider switching to `mpsc::channel` with a bounded capacity (e.g., `batch_size * (max_retries + 2)`), and either dropping events or applying backpressure when the channel is full.

**SSRF: webhook URL validation only checks for empty strings** (Medium)

The `validate()` method only rejects empty URLs. A URL like `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/` or `file:///etc/passwd` would pass validation. While webhook config is operator-controlled today, defense-in-depth is warranted — URL validation prevents future runtime misconfiguration or injection.

Consider parsing the URL at config-validation time to reject non-`http`/`https` schemes. The `llm_base_url_parts()` pattern in `agenthub.rs:1074-1093` demonstrates the approach.
Fixed — added 30s timeout on the oneshot await.
Fixed — signature is now computed once before the retry loop.
Fixed — split into normalize() + validate().
Acknowledged. Will address in a follow-up performance PR.
CubeAPI currently trusts operator-provided URLs across all config fields (AUTH_CALLBACK_URL, DATABASE_URL, etc.). Will revisit if the project adopts a unified URL validation policy.
Acknowledged. Deferring to a follow-up PR alongside circuit breaker.

**`flush()` blocks indefinitely during shutdown**

`flush()` awaits the oneshot reply with no timeout. If the delivery loop is stuck retrying (potentially ~21s+), this blocks `main.rs:330` during graceful shutdown past the SIGTERM deadline. Consider a timeout (e.g. 30s) on the oneshot await.

**Two small perf concerns on retries:**
1. `body.clone()` does a full heap copy of the serialized payload on each retry. Use `bytes::Bytes` for O(1) refcounted clones instead.
2. `sign_body()` is recomputed per retry but produces the same result. Compute once before the retry loop and reuse.

**`validate()` mutates state — consider `normalize()` + `validate()`**

Callers expect `validate()` to be read-only, but it also trims URLs, normalizes events, and filters blank HMAC secrets in-place. A future maintainer calling `cfg.validate()` mid-update may be surprised. Splitting into `normalize()` (no side effects) + `validate()` would clarify the contract.

**O(N×M) per-endpoint event clones**

For each endpoint this clones every matching `LogEvent` (contains `HashMap<String, Value>` — heap-heavy) into a new `Vec`. With M endpoints and N events, that's N×M heap copies. Consider collecting `Vec<&LogEvent>` (pointer copies) and serializing by reference instead.

**SSRF risk: no endpoint URL validation against private/internal IPs**

A misconfigured `CUBE_API_WEBHOOK_URL=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/` will have CubeAPI POST lifecycle events there with no restriction. Consider adding URL validation in `config/mod.rs::validate()` that rejects or warns about RFC 1918, loopback, and link-local IP ranges. Also consider warning on `http://` vs `https://` (CWE-319).

**Unbounded channel + sequential delivery risks OOM under backpressure**

Two compounding issues:

1. `mpsc::unbounded_channel` provides no backpressure. When endpoints are slow or retrying, `flush_buffer` blocks the delivery loop and events pile up in the channel without bound.

2. `flush_buffer` iterates endpoints sequentially (line 221). One slow endpoint delays all others. Default retries + timeout can stall the loop for ~21s per endpoint.

Suggestions:
- Use `mpsc::channel` (bounded, e.g. 2048 capacity) so handlers feel backpressure
- Dispatch per-endpoint deliveries concurrently via `join_all` or `tokio::spawn`
